The text says that SNPs with more than 30% missing data were removed, but the final SNP set contains SNPs with up to 31.7% missing data (40 SNPs above 30% over the 300 accessions; 155 over the 290 analysed). The likely reason is the order of the filters: the 30% filter was applied before genotypes supported by fewer than three reads were set to missing, which added missing calls afterwards. edits.old: [TODO - the pre-sowing treatment of the seeds. The text gives no details and cites Potapenko et al. 2026b (Mol Ecol), whose protocol is: seeds dried at 30 °C for 14 days, dipped in 4% sodium hypochlorite, sown in mid-October on germination paper, kept 10 days in the dark at 4 °C, then moved to 5-L pots with a commercial soil mix. The sources disagree: Potapenko et al. 2026a (Mol Biol Evol) gives a 3% chlorine solution, sowing trays, 10 days in the dark at 4 °C and 14 days in a growth chamber at 20 °C before transplanting; N. Pintel's thesis and our old drafts give 3% sodium hypochlorite for 5 minutes, a 5-minute rinse in distilled water and germination paper at 16 °C for 18 days. Please confirm which protocol was used in this experiment; if it differs from the cited paper, the details will be written here.]{.comment-start id="206" author="TODO"}[as described by Potapenko et al. edits.old: TODO - the wild-versus-cultivated comparison rests on one old paper. The sentence says that domestication and breeding moved cultivated barley toward higher starch and lower protein and fiber, citing only Friedman and Atsmon (1988), which could not be checked (no PDF or abstract available; see the reference comment in the Introduction). Our experiment grew two cultivated checks, Morex and Clipper, but they are not in the analysed data. N. Pintel's NIR files contain one scan of each, from 17 November 2020: Morex 7.0% protein, 64.7% starch, 4.1% beta-glucan and 2.7% fiber; Clipper 12.9%, 59.7%, 5.4% and 4.2%; the wild accessions averaged about 16% protein and 33-43% starch in the first two seasons. One scan per cultivar is too little to replace the citation, but it points the same way. Decide whether to keep the citation alone, add these values, or find a second source.
